component_edits.replacement: Implements the core audio pipeline for voice sessions. AudioEngine captures microphone input and manages playback; VAD and barge-in components detect and respond to user speech; caches and AudioPlaybackOrchestrator coordinate synthesized audio. Session and Knowledge Bowl flows use this module, which in turn connects to Telemetry, service protocols, TTS, and Voice. The component's mapped files and relationships provide the current measured detail.

tour_edits.expected: Once speech is detected, one of six STT providers streams a transcript. Which one handles the leg is a runtime choice — STTProviderRouter lives here, and GLMASRHealthMonitor tracks provider health — so a latency problem on this leg may be a provider problem, not a pipeline problem.
tour_edits.replacement: Once speech is detected, the selected STT implementation streams a transcript. Provider selection is a runtime choice — STTProviderRouter lives here, and GLMASRHealthMonitor tracks provider health — so a latency problem on this leg may be a provider problem, not a pipeline problem.

tour_edits.expected: The assembled context goes to one of the LLM providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, self-hosted, or on-device llama.cpp — each an actor streaming tokens via streamCompletion, with FallbackLLMService chaining providers on failure. Streaming matters: the TTS leg can start on early tokens rather than waiting for the full reply.
tour_edits.replacement: The assembled context goes to the selected LLM implementation — cloud, self-hosted, or on-device — and the observed provider actors expose streaming completion. A FallbackLLMService implementation exists in this component, but this static review did not establish that the current application constructs it. Streaming allows the TTS leg to begin before the full reply is available.

tour_edits.expected: Reply text streams into one of seven TTS providers, each returning an AsyncStream of audio chunks, with pronunciation hints applied first. From here audio flows back to the playback orchestrator in core/audio — closing the loop — where a barge-in can interrupt it and start the cycle again.
tour_edits.replacement: Reply text streams into the selected TTS implementation, with observed services returning asynchronous audio chunks and applying pronunciation hints. From here audio flows back to the playback orchestrator in core/audio — closing the loop — where a barge-in can interrupt it and start the cycle again.

tour_edits.step_title: LLM providers plus a fallback chain
tour_edits.expected: The LLM side adds two things the other legs don't have: an on-device llama.cpp path with its own model manager, and FallbackLLMService, which chains providers so a failed call degrades to the next tier instead of failing the turn.
tour_edits.replacement: The LLM side includes an on-device llama.cpp path with its own model manager and a FallbackLLMService implementation. The implementation can chain providers, but this static review did not find evidence that the current application constructs that fallback service at runtime.
